blockDefinitions.description: Turns the denoised rows of the packed sequence back into latents: drops the conditioning rows the loop never wrote, then unpacks the video rows into `(1, latent_channels, num_latent_frames, latent_height, latent_width)` and the channel-major audio rows into the `(2, audio_latent_channels, num_audio_latents)` the mono audio VAE consumes. The decoders then take latents from any source, and popping them leaves latents in hand.

inputs.name: num_condition_audio_rows

blockDefinitions.description: Denormalizes the generated audio latents and decodes them into a stereo waveform, truncated to the video's length when `num_frames` is known: the audio latents cover whole 25 ms hops, so the decoded soundtrack runs a few milliseconds past the last frame. blockDefinitions.description: Media preparation block. - `PikaH3FlexRef2VASetupStep` runs when `references` is provided (`ref2va`): it resolves the plan and normalizes every reference onto the model's own rates and the resolutions of the canvas' tier. - `PikaH3FlexResizeStep` runs when a keyframe is provided (`fl2va`), center-cropping and resizing the keyframes onto the target canvas. - a text-only request (`t2va`) skips this block, and the layout step falls back to the 768p 16:9 canvas.

inputs.name: references
inputs.description: The references to condition on, **in the order the model should read them**: the order labels them in the prompt presentation and lays them out on the shared rotary clock, so a different order is a different request. One dataclass per modality, all holding in-memory media — a [`PikaH3FlexImageReference`] (at most 9), a [`PikaH3FlexVideoReference`] at its own `fps` (at most 3, whose `audio` soundtrack is conditioned on as well), or a [`PikaH3FlexAudioReference`] at its own `sample_rate` (at most 3) — for at most 12 references in total, and audio references cannot be the only ones. Every video or standalone audio reference runs 2 to 15 seconds, and the video durations and the standalone audio durations each sum to at most 15 seconds. These blocks never open a media file: decode with each class's `from_file` classmethod, which brings the rates along.

blockDefinitions.description: Encodes the `ref2va` references — image and video references through the video VAE, soundtracks through the audio VAE. They are the anchors of the whole denoising loop, which only ever writes the generated rows; the prepare-latents step noises the visual ones to MiniMax-H3's conditioning level and packs them, while soundtracks ride along clean at `t = 1.0`. The latent geometry of every reference is the shape of what this emits, which is what the packed layout is built from.

inputs.description: The references normalized by the setup step, in packed order.

outputs.name: condition_latents
outputs.description: The encoded video conditioning latents of the image and video references, one `(1, latent_channels, num_latent_frames, latent_height, latent_width)` tensor each in packed order, or None when the references carry none.

outputs.name: audio_condition_latents
outputs.description: The clean audio conditioning rows of the reference soundtracks, one `(num_audio_latents * 2, audio_latent_channels)` tensor per audio-bearing reference in packed order. One entry per reference rather than one concatenated block, because the packed layout is built from the row count of each.

blockDefinitions.description: Resolves the `ref2va` plan — the canvas (Pika H3 Flex's own 16:9 unless asked otherwise; references never bind the generated geometry) and the `17 * n + 5` frame count — and normalizes every reference onto the model's own rates and the resolutions of the canvas' tier: an image reference is encoded at the tier's reference short edge (1024 pixels below the 768 tier, 2048 from it upwards) and a video reference is put on the tier's own canvas rule.

inputs.name: references
inputs.description: The references to condition on, **in the order the model should read them**: the order labels them in the prompt presentation and lays them out on the shared rotary clock, so a different order is a different request. One dataclass per modality, all holding in-memory media — a [`PikaH3FlexImageReference`] (at most 9), a [`PikaH3FlexVideoReference`] at its own `fps` (at most 3, whose `audio` soundtrack is conditioned on as well), or a [`PikaH3FlexAudioReference`] at its own `sample_rate` (at most 3) — for at most 12 references in total, and audio references cannot be the only ones. Every video or standalone audio reference runs 2 to 15 seconds, and the video durations and the standalone audio durations each sum to at most 15 seconds. These blocks never open a media file: decode with each class's `from_file` classmethod, which brings the rates along.

inputs.description: Height of the generated video in pixels, a multiple of 32.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Width of the generated video in pixels, a multiple of 32.

inputs.name: num_frames
inputs.description: Number of frames to generate, at the fixed 24 fps: 120 to 360, i.e. 5 to 15 seconds, snapped up to the next `17 * n + 5` the video VAE can decode. To generate a video as long as a reference soundtrack, pass `round(samples / sample_rate * 24)`.

The canvas resolved here is the one the whole request generates at.

blockDefinitions.description: Initializes the two six-step schedules from the pipeline's `denoising_step_list` config — the sigmas the released adapters were trained for, which each scheduler pushes through its shift (`12.0` for video, `3.0` for audio) — and stages the row-to-timestep plan of every step. One forward serves every modality and every noise level at once: the generated rows step down their own schedule while the conditioning rows stay pinned at their noise-augmentation level, and that assignment is static per step. There is no `num_inference_steps`: the step count is the adapter's, fixed by the schedule.
